strongest_angle: An October 2026 super El Nino weather pattern delivered heavy rainfall across South America, sending near-record water volumes surging over Iguazu Falls on the border between Argentina and Brazil.

key_facts.fact: The Rio Iguazu reached 17,700 cubic metres per second at Iguazu Falls in October 2026, which is nearly twelve times the average flow.
Heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate, leading national park officials in Argentina to temporarily restrict tourist access.
Iguazu Falls spans more than a mile across both Argentina and Brazil, featuring a complex of cascades that experienced severe flooding due to El Nino.
The heavy rains and subsequent floods forced the temporary closure of the Circuito Superior walkway for tourists at Iguazu National Park.
